INSERT INTO "app_version" VALUES('2XzB3rKi0QljeDzN32bEXzbyksY',0,'40','25Wg8fHYuNVbV82S6rcMlyRYQGh','Stable',NULL,1699622223,'1.7.0',0,'# KNIME Business Hub 1.7.0
## Important installation notes
Kubernetes version 1.25-1.27 is required for Business Hub 1.7.0. Pre-flight checks in the installer make sure that the correct version is available.
## Infrastructure and security updates
### Support provided ingress-nginx deployments
- In existing clusters creating own ingress-nginx deployments before the installation of Hub is now enabled. Wether the Hub install process deploys the inbuilt ingress-nginx can be configured on the Kots Admin dashboard.
### Security context update
- Security contexts updated for pods, containers and jobs in the hub, knime and knime-execution namespaces.
## Bugfixes
- Fixed a bug where schedules edited with KNIME Analytics Platform didn’t respect job discard settings.
- Fixed a bug where saving executed job as workflows didn’t work in case workflow size was larger than 50 MB.
- Fixed a bug where under certain circumstances jobs were shown duplicated in the AP explorer.
- Fixed a bug where schedules in all teams connected to a user were deactivated when the user left any team.
- Various smaller fixes.','apiVersion: troubleshoot.sh/v1beta2
kind: Collector
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null

spec:
  collectors:
  - clusterInfo: {}
  - clusterResources: {}
  - logs:

        maxAge: 30d
        maxLines: 10000
        sinceTime: null
      name: logs/hub-namespace
      namespace: hub
      selector: null
  - logs:
      limits:
        maxAge: 30d
        maxLines: 10000
        sinceTime: null
      name: logs/knime-namespace
      namespace: knime
      selector: null
  - logs:
      limits:
        maxAge: 30d
        maxLines: 10000
        sinceTime: null
      name: logs/{{repl ConfigOption "execution_context_namespace" | TrimSpace }}-namespace
      namespace: repl{{ ConfigOption "execution_context_namespace" | TrimSpace }}
      selector: null
  - logs:
      limits:
        maxAge: 30d
        maxLines: 10000
        sinceTime: null
      name: logs/istio-system-namespace
      namespace: istio-system
      selector: null
status: {}
','apiVersion: troubleshoot.sh/v1beta2
kind: Preflight
metadata:
  annotations:
    kots.io/exclude: "true"
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: preflight-checks
spec:
  analyzers:
  - clusterVersion:
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Kubernetes versions v1.25 - v1.27.
          uri: https://www.kubernetes.io
          when: ''>= 1.28.0''
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Kubernetes versions v1.25 - v1.27.
          uri: https://kubernetes.io
          when: < 1.25.0
      - pass:
          message: Your cluster meets the recommended and required versions of Kubernetes.
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: KOTS Admin Console Version
      fileName: static/kots-version
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports KOTS v1.101.2+. Please upgrade the
            KOTS based on the upgrade documentation.
          uri: https://docs.knime.com/latest/business_hub_installation_guide/index.html#_introduction
          when: "false"
      - pass:
          message: Your cluster meets the required version of KOTS.
          when: "true"
      regex: ^true$
  - containerRuntime:
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: Docker container runtime was found.
          when: == docker
      - pass:
          message: Containerd runtime was found.
          when: == containerd
      - pass:
          message: CRI-O runtime was found.
          when: == cri-o
      - fail:
          message: Did not find a viable container runtime (e.g. Docker).
  - distribution:
      checkName: Check Kubernetes environment.
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: The application does not support Microk8s clusters.
          when: == microk8s
      - warn:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Minikube clusters for testing only.
          when: == minikube
      - pass:
          message: EKS is a supported distribution.
          when: == eks
      - pass:
          message: GKE is a supported distribution.
          when: == gke
      - pass:
          message: AKS is a supported distribution.
          when: == aks
      - pass:
          message: K3s is a supported distribution.
          when: == k3s
      - pass:
          message: KURL is a supported distribution.
          when: == kurl
      - pass:
          message: Openshift is a supported distribution.
          when: == openShift
  - nodeResources:
      checkName: Total CPU Cores in the cluster is 16 or greater.
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: The cluster must contain at least 16 cores.
          when: sum(cpuCapacity) < 16
      - pass:
          message: There are at least 16 cores in the cluster.
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: PostgreSQL configuration
      fileName: static/postgres-settings
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: PostgreSQL configuration has no syntax errors.
          when: "true"
      - fail:
          message: PostgreSQL configuration has non-numeric values!
          when: "false"
      regex: ''[1-9][0-9]*;[1-9][0-9]*;[1-9][0-9]*''
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: KNIME Business Hub URL validation
      fileName: static/base-url
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: URL passes validation for alphanumeric and special characters.
          when: "true"
      - fail:
          message: Invalid URL. The URL cannot contain spaces or slashes /, and needs
            to have a top-level domain and at least one subdomain.
          when: "false"
      regex: ^[^\/ ]+\.[^\/ ]+$
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: ''KNIME Business Hub URL validation: IP address''
      fileName: static/base-url
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: URL is not an IP address.
          when: "false"
      - fail:
          message: Invalid URL. The URL cannot be an IP address.
          when: "true"
      regex: ^(?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$
  collectors:
  - data:
      data: 200;1000;1024
      name: static/postgres-settings
  - data:
      data: hub.kbh-troubleshooting.com
      name: static/base-url
  - data:
      data: "true"
      name: static/kots-version
status: {}

kind: Application
metadata:
  annotations:
    kots.io/exclude: "true"
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: knime-hub
spec:
  additionalImages:
  - ghcr.io/zalando/spilo-15:3.0-p1
  - registry.opensource.zalan.do/acid/pgbouncer:master-27
  - registry.opensource.zalan.do/acid/logical-backup:v1.10.0
  - curlimages/curl:8.2.1
  - k8s.gcr.io/ingress-nginx/controller:v1.3.1
  - quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:19.0.3-legacy
  - registry.hubdev.knime.com/knime-hub/knime-hub-keycloak-extensions-init:19.0.3-legacy-00851e8
  - docker.io/istio/pilot:1.18.1
  - docker.io/istio/proxyv2:1.18.1
  - docker.io/istio/install-cni:1.18.1
  - registry.hub.knime.com/knime/knime-full:r-5.1.1-379
  - adoptopenjdk/openjdk11:x86_64-ubuntu-jre-11.0.18_10
  additionalNamespaces:
  - knime
  - istio-system
  - ''*''
  branding:
    css:
    - ./custom.css
  icon: data:image/png;base64,
  kubectlVersion: latest
  kustomizeVersion: latest
  releaseNotes: |-
    # KNIME Business Hub 1.7.0
    ## Important installation notes
    Kubernetes version 1.25-1.27 is required for Business Hub 1.7.0. Pre-flight checks in the installer make sure that the correct version is available.
    ## Infrastructure and security updates
    ### Support provided ingress-nginx deployments
    - In existing clusters creating own ingress-nginx deployments before the installation of Hub is now enabled. Wether the Hub install process deploys the inbuilt ingress-nginx can be configured on the Kots Admin dashboard.
    ### Security context update
    - Security contexts updated for pods, containers and jobs in the hub, knime and knime-execution namespaces.
    ## Bugfixes
    - Fixed a bug where schedules edited with KNIME Analytics Platform didn’t respect job discard settings.
    - Fixed a bug where saving executed job as workflows didn’t work in case workflow size was larger than 50 MB.
    - Fixed a bug where under certain circumstances jobs were shown duplicated in the AP explorer.
    - Fixed a bug where schedules in all teams connected to a user were deactivated when the user left any team.
    - Various smaller fixes.
  statusInformers:
  - hub/deployment/accounts-service
  - hub/deployment/catalog-service
  - hub/deployment/hub-webapp
  - hub/deployment/search-service
  - hub/deployment/search-sync-service
  - ''{{repl if ConfigOption "enable_notification_svc" | ParseBool}}hub/deployment/notification-service{{repl
    else}}{{repl end}}''
  - ''{{repl if ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed"}}knime/deployment/ingress-nginx-controller{{repl
    else}}{{repl end}}''
  - knime/statefulset/keycloak
  title: KNIME Business Hub
status: {}

  - image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak-operator:19.0.3-legacy
  - image: registry.hubdev.knime.com/knime-hub/knime-hub-execution-state-persistor:2.1.1-stable-0010-3376f3b
    isPrivate: true
  - image: registry.hubdev.knime.com/knime-hub/knime-hub-accounts-service:2.1.1-stable-0010-27fcc6a
    isPrivate: true
  - image: registry.hubdev.knime.com/knime-hub/knime-hub-secret-store:1.0.0-beta-20231101-174905-000230-be52b25
    isPrivate: true
  releaseNotes: |-
    # KNIME Business Hub 1.7.0
    ## Important installation notes
    Kubernetes version 1.25-1.27 is required for Business Hub 1.7.0. Pre-flight checks in the installer make sure that the correct version is available.
    ## Infrastructure and security updates
    ### Support provided ingress-nginx deployments
    - In existing clusters creating own ingress-nginx deployments before the installation of Hub is now enabled. Wether the Hub install process deploys the inbuilt ingress-nginx can be configured on the Kots Admin dashboard.
    ### Security context update
    - Security contexts updated for pods, containers and jobs in the hub, knime and knime-execution namespaces.
    ## Bugfixes
    - Fixed a bug where schedules edited with KNIME Analytics Platform didn’t respect job discard settings.
    - Fixed a bug where saving executed job as workflows didn’t work in case workflow size was larger than 50 MB.
    - Fixed a bug where under certain circumstances jobs were shown duplicated in the AP explorer.
    - Fixed a bug where schedules in all teams connected to a user were deactivated when the user left any team.
    - Various smaller fixes.
  replicatedProxyDomain: proxy.replicated.com
  replicatedRegistryDomain: registry.replicated.com
  updateCursor: "40"
  versionLabel: 1.7.0
status: {}

','apiVersion: kots.io/v1beta1
kind: Config
metadata:
  annotations:
    kots.io/exclude: "true"
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: config
spec:
  groups:
  - description: High-level settings for the KNIME Business Hub deployment.
    items:
    - default: KNIME Business Hub
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub deployment name is displayed in several places
        in the web UI. The value may contain spaces.
      name: knime_hub_name
      required: true
      title: KNIME Business Hub Deployment Name
      type: text
      value: KNIME Business Hub
    - default: knime-business-hub
      help_text: Name of the Mountpoint ID when adding this KNIME Business Hub deployment
        in the KNIME AP. The value may not contain spaces (it is recommended to use
        dashes `-` instead).
      name: knime_hub_mountpoint_id
      required: true
      title: KNIME Business Hub Mountpoint ID
      type: text
      value: knime-business-hub
    - default: ""
      help_text: Upload your KNIME Business Hub License `.xml` file. You have received
        this file from your account manager, in addition to the Replicated License
        `.yaml` file that you used during a previous step. Contact your KNIME account
        manager if you have not yet received a `.xml` file containing the KNIME Business
        Hub License.
      name: knime_license_xml
      required: true
      title: KNIME Business Hub License
      type: file
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      name: knime_license_xml_wrong_file_ending
      title: ''***Invalid file extension! Please upload the KNIME Business Hub License,
        which is an `.xml` file.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl and (not (regexMatch "^.*\\.xml$" (ConfigOptionFilename "knime_license_xml")))
        (not (ConfigOptionEquals "knime_license_xml" "")) }}''
    - default: "0"
      name: enable_advanced_settings
      title: View Advanced Settings
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ eq ( LicenseFieldValue "licenseType" ) "dev" }}
    name: deployment_name
    title: Global
  - description: KNIME Business Hub URLs that will be referenced across all services
      and deployments. You need to provide DNS entries for all of these.
    items:
    - default: hub.example.com
      help_text: The URL to the KNIME Business Hub web app. Omit the `http://` or
        `https://` scheme.
      name: knime_hub_webapp_url
      required: true
      title: Webapp URL
      type: text
      value: hub.example.com
    - default: ""
      name: knime_hub_webapp_url_invalid
      title: |-
        ***Invalid URL. The URL cannot contain spaces or slashes `/`, and needs to have a top-level domain and at least one subdomain.***
        *Valid examples:*
        `hub.example.com`
        `example.com`
        *Invalid examples:*
        `https://hub.example.com/`
        `example.com/hub`
        `myhub`
        `.myhub.com`
        `myhub.`
        `***HIDDEN***`
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[^\\/ ]+\\.[^\\/ ]+$" (ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url"))
        }}''
    - default: ""
      name: knime_hub_webapp_url_is_ip
      title: |-
        ***Invalid URL. The URL cannot be an IP address.***
        *Valid examples:*
        `hub.example.com`
        `example.com`
        *Invalid examples:*
        `https://hub.example.com/`
        `example.com/hub`
        `myhub`
        `.myhub.com`
        `myhub.`
        `***HIDDEN***`
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl (regexMatch "^(?:[0-9]{1,3}\\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$" (ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url"))
        }}''
    - default: ""
      help_text: The URL for KNIME Business Hub DataApps.
      name: knime_hub_dataapps_url
      readonly: true
      title: DataApps URL
      type: text
      value: apps.{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_execution_services" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The URL to the KNIME Business Hub API.
      name: knime_hub_api_url
      readonly: true
      title: API URL
      type: text
      value: api.{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The URL to the KNIME Business Hub authentication endpoint.
      name: knime_hub_auth_url
      readonly: true
      title: Authentication URL
      type: text
      value: auth.{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The URL to the KNIME Business Hub persistent storage endpoint.
      name: knime_hub_storage_url
      readonly: true
      title: Storage URL
      type: text
      value: storage.{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_minio" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The URL to the KNIME Business Hub embedded registry endpoint. This
        can be used to host custom KNIME Executor docker images.
      name: knime_hub_registry_url
      readonly: true
      title: Registry URL
      type: text
      value: registry.{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOption "enable_embedded_registry" | ParseBool) IsKurl
        }}
    name: urls
    title: URLs
  - description: Configuration for external load balancer and TLS.
    items:
    - default: managed
      help_text: Select how `Ingress` is managed for KNIME Business Hub. Use ''Managed''
        if an Ingress controller should be deployed and managed by KNIME Business
        Hub. Use ''Provided'' if an Ingress controller already exists in the cluster.
        If the Ingress Controller is provided, all needed `Ingress` resources will
        need to be manually created. See [documentation_link] for more information.
        When ''Managed'', the [Ingress-NGINX controller](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/)
        is deployed and serves as a reverse proxy and load balancer for entry to the
        cluster.
      items:
      - default: ""
        name: managed
        title: Managed by KNIME Business Hub
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: provided
        title: Provided by the cluster
        value: ""
      name: ingress_controller
      title: Ingress Controller Configuration
      type: select_one
      value: ""
    - default: "0"
      help_text: ''**(Deprecated)** Deploy an external load balancer. Your cloud provider
        and kubernetes distribution (e.g., AWS EKS or Azure AKS) must support automatic
        load balancer provisioning in order for this feature to take effect. See [kubernetes
        documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#loadbalancer)
        for more. This option only sets the Ingress `Service` to type `LoadBalancer`.''
      name: enable_load_balancer
      title: Deploy Load Balancer
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed" }}
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Enable Transport Layer Security (TLS). This option is highly recommended
        for any KNIME Business Hub deployed in a production environment. A certificate
        must be created for all URLs configured above, including a wildcard certificate
        for `{{repl ConfigOption "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}` and `*.{{repl ConfigOption
        "knime_hub_webapp_url" }}`.
      name: enable_tls
      recommended: true
      title: Enable TLS
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: external
      help_text: Select the TLS certificate authority to use for KNIME Business Hub.
      items:
      - default: ""
        name: external
        title: Upload your own certificate
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: existing_secret
        title: Existing TLS Secret
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: aws
        title: AWS ACM Certificate
        value: ""
      name: tls_cert_authority
      title: TLS Certificate Configuration
      type: select_one
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The private key file should be pem formatted.
      name: tls_private_key_file
      title: Private Key File
      type: file
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) (ConfigOptionEquals "tls_cert_authority" "external")
        }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: The certificate file should be the full certificate chain in pem
        format.
      name: tls_certificate_file
      title: Certificate File
      type: file
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) (ConfigOptionEquals "tls_cert_authority" "external")
        }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: Specify the name of an existing Secret of type `kubernetes.io/tls`
        in the `knime` namespace. It needs to have keys `tls.crt` and `tls.key`. See
        [ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/tls/)
        and [kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/secret/#tls-secrets)
        for more. This option is recommended if you have an automatic process that
        can create and update `kubernetes.io/tls` Secrets in the cluster.
      name: tls_certificate_secret_name
      title: Existing TLS Secret
      type: text
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) (ConfigOptionEquals "tls_cert_authority" "existing_secret")
        }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: ''When deploying in an existing AWS EKS cluster, and selecting the
        loadbalancer option above, you can attach a certificate from the AWS Certificate
        Manager to the loadbalancer here. Set the certificate ARN below in the format:
        arn:aws:acm:<region>:<account-id>:certificate/<certificate-id>''
      name: tls_aws_acm_cert
      title: AWS Certificate Manager ARN
      type: text
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) (ConfigOptionEquals "tls_cert_authority" "aws")
        }}
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Customize the ingress proxy behavior such as read/send/connect timeouts.
        Changes to these settings require a restart of the `ingress-nginx-controller`
        pod before taking effect.
      name: enable_ingress_config
      title: Show Advanced Ingress Configuration
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
        "enable_tls" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Customize the [Istio service mesh](https://istio.io/).
      name: enable_advanced_istio_config
      title: Show Advanced Istio Configuration
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Enable the addition of a custom CA certificate. Some organizations
        may use their own CA, and adding it here will allow certain KNIME Business
        Hub services to communicate with external resources that require a custom
        CA.
      name: enable_custom_ca_certificate
      title: Enable Custom Certificate Authority (CA) Certificate
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      help_text: Provide CA certificate content in PEM format. Multiple CAs can be
        added to this textarea.
      name: custom_ca_certificate
      required: true
      title: Custom Certificate Authority (CA) Certificate
      type: textarea
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_custom_ca_certificate" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: "1"
      help_text: ''Enable the Core DNS Updater Job. This job re-routes any external
        calls to KNIME Business Hub endpoints such as `auth.hub.example.com` and `api.hub.example.com`
        back to the Ingress-NGINX controller. **Please note: this setting has no effect
        on existing cluster installations (the Core DNS Updater Job will always be
        disabled in existing cluster installations).**''
      name: enable_core_dns_updater
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Core DNS Updater Job
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ eq ( LicenseFieldValue "show-coredns-job-disable-option" ) "true"
        }}
    name: networking
    title: Networking
  - description: Advanced configuration for the Ingress-NGINX controller.
    items:
    - default: "1800"
      help_text: Proxy read timeout (seconds). This setting will affect the maximum
        size of content uploaded to KNIME Business Hub.
      name: ingress_read_timeout
      title: Read Timeout
      type: text
      value: "1800"
    - default: ""
      name: ingress_read_timeout_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "ingress_read_timeout"))
        }}''
    - default: "1800"
      help_text: Proxy send timeout (seconds). This setting will affect the maximum
        size of content downloaded from KNIME Business Hub.
      name: ingress_send_timeout
      title: Send Timeout
      type: text
      value: "1800"
    - default: ""
      name: ingress_send_timeout_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "ingress_send_timeout"))
        }}''
    - default: "60"
      help_text: Proxy connect timeout (seconds).
      name: ingress_connect_timeout
      title: Connect Timeout
      type: text
      value: "60"
    - default: ""
      name: ingress_connect_timeout_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "ingress_connect_timeout"))
        }}''
    - default: "0"
      help_text: The maximum allowed size of the client request body, in megabytes.
        This setting will affect the maximum size of content uploaded to KNIME Business
        Hub. Setting this value to `0` disables checking of the client request body
        size.
      name: ingress_max_client_body_size
      title: Maximum Client Request Body Size
      type: text
      value: "0"
    - default: ""
      name: ingress_body_size_timeout_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[0-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "ingress_max_client_body_size"))
        }}''
    - default: ""
      name: whitespace
      title: '' ''
      type: label
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: |-
        If enabled then use-forwarded-headers is set to true in Ingress-NGINX: https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/nginx-configuration/configmap/#use-forwarded-headers

        In almost all scenarios this should be left enabled.
      name: nginx_use_forwarded_headers
      title: use-forwarded-headers in Ingress-NGINX
      type: bool
      value: ""
    name: networking_ingress
    title: ''Networking: Ingress''
    when: repl{{ and (ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed") (ConfigOption
      "enable_ingress_config" | ParseBool) }}
  - description: Advanced configuration for the [Istio service mesh](https://istio.io/).
    items:
    - default: "1"
      help_text: ''The [Istio service mesh](https://istio.io/) manages network traffic
        for KNIME Business Hub deployments. Its functionality depends on the Ingress-NGINX
        Controller. **Please note: it is highly recommended to leave this option enabled.**''
      name: enable_istio
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Istio
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ eq (LicenseFieldValue "licenseType") "dev" }}
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: enable_legacy_istio_chart
      title: Enable Legacy Istio Chart
      type: bool
      value: repl{{ if (eq Sequence 0) }}repl{{ printf "0" }}repl{{ else }}repl{{
        printf "1" }}repl{{ end }}
      when: "false"
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Istio Ingress Gateway](https://istio.io/latest/docs/concepts/traffic-management/#gateways)
        allows Istio to manage traffic entering the cluster.
      name: enable_istio_ingressgateway
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Istio Ingress Gateway
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (eq (LicenseFieldValue "licenseType" ) "dev") (ConfigOption
        "enable_istio" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: "0"
      help_text: The [Istio Egress Gateway](https://istio.io/latest/docs/concepts/traffic-management/#gateways)
        allows Istio to manage traffic exiting the cluster.
      name: enable_istio_egressgateway
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Istio Egress Gateway
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ and (eq (LicenseFieldValue "licenseType") "dev") (ConfigOption
        "enable_istio" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: false
      help_text: ''The [Istio CNI Plugin](https://istio.io/latest/docs/setup/additional-setup/cni/)
        removes the need for privileged istio-init containers which require root access
        and elevated privileges. This is useful for ensuring maximum compliance with
        strict cluster security policies. **Please note: This option is experimental
        and may not work with all Kubernetes distributions (known issues exist with
        OpenShift and GKE). If this setting is changed, all deployments in the `hub`
        and `hub-execution` namespaces will need to be restarted for the changes to
        Istio to take effect. The `kubectl rollout restart deployment -n hub && kubectl
        delete pods --all --namespace hub-execution` command can be used to restart
        relevant deployments and execution contexts.**''
      name: enable_istio_cni_plugin
      title: Enable Istio CNI Plugin (experimental)
      type: bool
      value: false
      when: repl{{ ConfigOption "enable_istio" | ParseBool }}
    name: networking_istio
    title: ''Networking: Istio''
    when: repl{{ ConfigOption "enable_advanced_istio_config" | ParseBool }}
  - description: KNIME Business Hub uses [Minio](https://min.io/) as an object store
      for workflows, avatars, and job data.
    items:
    - default: 100Gi
      help_text: ''The size of the volume attached to each Minio pod. Examples: `5Gi`,
        `5000Mi`, `1Ti`.''
      name: minio_volume_size
      required: true
      title: Volume Size
      type: text
      value: 100Gi
    name: object_storage
    title: Object Storage
    when: repl{{ and (ConfigOption "enable_minio" | ParseBool) (or (not IsKurl) (KurlOption
      "rook.version" | ParseBool)) }}
  - description: KNIME Business Hub uses [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/)
      to store metadata about users, workflows, jobs, and more. You can fine tune
      PostgreSQL performance below. Changing settings here may trigger a restart of
      the PostgreSQL instance.
    items:
    - default: "200"
      help_text: Number of [maximum concurrent connections](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-connection.html)
        that PostgreSQL allows.
      name: postgres_max_connections
      title: Max Connections
      type: text
      value: "200"
    - default: ""
      name: postgres_max_connections_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "postgres_max_connections"))
        }}''
    - default: "1000"
      help_text: In millicores, 1000m = 1 CPU core. See [kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/).
      name: postgres_resources_cpu
      title: CPU Resources
      type: text
      value: "1000"
    - default: ""
      name: postgres_resources_cpu_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "postgres_resources_cpu"))
        }}''
    - default: "1024"
      help_text: In megabytes. See [kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/).
      name: postgres_resources_memory
      title: Memory Resources
      type: text
      value: "1024"
    - default: ""
      name: postgres_resources_memory_non_numeric
      title: ''***Please enter only numeric values in the field above.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*$" (ConfigOption "postgres_resources_memory"))
        }}''
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Enable the database that can be used by the KNIME Continuous Deployment
        for Data Science (CDDS) extension. The activation of this option is necessary
        only if you intend to use the CDDS extension in conjunction with the Hub''s
        internal database. See [installation guide of CDDS](https://docs.knime.com/latest/business_hub_cdds_guide/index.html#installation_guide).
      name: enable_cdds_postgres_database
      title: Enable CDDS database
      type: bool
      value: ""
    name: postgres
    title: PostgreSQL Database
    when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_postgres_operator" | ParseBool) }}
  - description: Configuration for an Embedded Registry for pushing and pulling custom
      KNIME execution docker images.
    items:
    - default: repl{{ if IsKurl }}repl{{ printf "1" }}repl{{ else }}repl{{ printf
        "0" }}repl{{ end }}
      name: enable_embedded_registry
      title: Enable Embedded Registry
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      name: embedded_registry_credentials_help
      title: Use the credentials below to authenticate your Docker CLI for pushing
        images to the registry. An image pull secret for executors is created automatically
        in the cluster.
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_embedded_registry" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: knime
      name: embedded_registry_username
      title: Embedded Registry Username
      type: text
      value: knime
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_embedded_registry" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      name: embedded_registry_password
      required: true
      title: Embedded Registry Password
      type: password
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_embedded_registry" | ParseBool) }}
    name: embedded-registry
    title: Embedded Registry
    when: repl{{ IsKurl }}
  - description: Customize the appearance of KNIME Business Hub.
    items:
    - default: "0"
      name: enable_branding
      title: Enable Branding Options
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      help_text: The image will be scaled to fit 183px wide and 48px high logo area.
        Images with significantly more height than width may appear small when displayed.
      name: logo_svg
      title: Custom Logo SVG File
      type: file
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_branding" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      name: logo_svg_invalid_extension
      title: ''***Invalid file extension! Please upload an `.svg` file.***''
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl and (not (regexMatch "^.*\\.svg$" (ConfigOptionFilename "logo_svg")))
        (not (ConfigOptionEquals "logo_svg" "")) }}''
    name: branding
    title: Branding
  - description: Configuration for the initial import of nodes and extensions to KNIME
      Business Hub.
    items:
    - default: "1"
      help_text: Enable an initial import of nodes and extensions to the KNIME Business
        Hub instance upon first installation.
      name: enable_importing_nodes_and_extensions
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Importing Nodes and Extensions
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Filter the initial import of nodes and extensions to trusted Update
        Sites only.
      name: trusted_update_sites_only
      title: Import from Trusted Update Sites Only
      type: bool
      value: ""
    name: nodes_and_extensions
    title: Nodes and Extensions
  - description: Configuration for the KNIME Business Hub notification service, which
      distributes email notifications for various events.
    items:
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Connect KNIME Business Hub to your mail server.
      name: enable_notification_svc
      recommended: true
      title: Enable Notifications
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: Enable to allow HTML in email notifications, or disable for plain
        text.
      name: notification_enable_html
      recommended: true
      title: Enable HTML in Email Notifications
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_notification_svc" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: ""
      help_text: ''Enter configuration properties for the Jakarta Mail library used
        by the Notification Service below. Consult the KNIME Business Hub Installation
        Guide, or see the Jakarta Mail API documentation for all possible parameters:
        https://jakarta.ee/specifications/mail/1.6/apidocs/index.html''
      name: notification_mail_server_config
      title: Mail Server Configuration
      type: textarea
      value: |
        mail.from=hub.email@example.com (KNIME Business Hub)
        mail.smtp.host=<host>
        mail.smtp.port=25
        mail.smtp.auth=true
        mail.smtp.user=<user>
        mail.password=<password>
        mail.smtp.starttls.enable=false
        mail.smtp.ssl.enable=false
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_notification_svc" | ParseBool) }}
    name: notifications
    title: Notifications
  - description: KNIME Business Hub uses Execution Contexts for hosting and executing
      KNIME workflows.
    items:
    - default: hub-execution
      help_text: The Kubernetes namespace for all new Execution Contexts. It is **highly**
        recommended to leave this option set to the default value.
      name: execution_context_namespace
      title: Execution Context Namespace
      type: text
      value: hub-execution
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Enable the use of custom execution images that require Docker authentication
        to pull.
      name: enable_custom_image_pull_secret
      title: Enable Custom Execution Image Pull Secret
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: regcred
      help_text: The name of the Kubernetes Secret resource which contains the Docker
        image pull secret for custom execution image(s). The secret should exist in
        the namespace defined in the **Execution Context Namespace** config option.
      name: execution_image_pull_secret
      title: Execution Image Pull Secret Name
      type: text
      value: regcred
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_custom_image_pull_secret" | ParseBool) }}
    - default: Recreate
      help_text: The `Recreate` strategy involves terminating and recreating execution
        contexts when they are updated. This may cause downtime but reduces the possibility
        of resource allocation conflicts during provisioning. On the other hand, the
        `Rolling Update` strategy brings a new execution context with updated configuration
        online before terminating the previous version, minimizing downtime. This
        strategy is often used to prevent misconfigured execution contexts from causing
        downtime for end users. Although `Rolling Update` is effective for minimizing
        downtime, `Recreate` is a better strategy for minimizing resource utilization.
        For more information on deployment strategies, please refer to the [Kubernetes
        documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/#strategy).
      items:
      - default: ""
        name: RollingUpdate
        title: Rolling Update
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: Recreate
        title: Recreate
        value: ""
      name: executor_deployment_strategy
      title: Execution Context Update Strategy
      type: select_one
      value: ""
    name: execution_contexts
    title: Execution Contexts
    when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_execution_services" | ParseBool) }}
  - description: Configuration for KNIME Edge.
    items:
    - default: "0"
      help_text: Enabling this option turns on the KNIME Hub Edge Service, which provides
        an integration point for the KNIME Edge Hub Adapter.
      name: enable_edge_service
      title: Enable KNIME Edge
      type: bool
      value: ""
    name: edge
    title: KNIME Edge
    when: repl{{ eq ( LicenseFieldValue "knime-edge-enabled" ) "true" }}
  - description: This section contains settings for browser security.
    items:
    - default: "1"
      help_text: Enabling this option allows you to set a custom Content Security
        Policy for Data Apps below. If disabled, no Content Security Policy header
        is set.
      name: enable_execution_webapp_csp_statement
      title: Enable Content Security Policy for Data Apps
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: default-src ''self''; script-src ''unsafe-inline'' ''unsafe-eval'' ''self'';
        style-src ''unsafe-inline'' ''self''; img-src ''self'' data:; font-src ''self'' data:;
      help_text: Specifies a custom Content Security Policy for Data App execution.
        It may be necessary to override the default if you are using BIRT report generators
        or custom JavaScript views that load external resources. The default works
        for all standard KNIME views. For more information about how to write the
        CSP statement, please refer to this [resource](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy).
      name: execution_webapp_csp_statement
      title: Content Security Policy for Data Apps
      type: text
      value: default-src ''self''; script-src ''unsafe-inline'' ''unsafe-eval'' ''self'';
        style-src ''unsafe-inline'' ''self''; img-src ''self'' data:; font-src ''self'' data:;
      when: repl{{ (ConfigOptionEquals "enable_execution_webapp_csp_statement" "1")
        }}
    - default: SAMEORIGIN
      help_text: Sets the `X-Frame-Options` header to the selected option, or doesn''t
        set the header if `none` is selected. This header is used to avoid click-jacking
        attacks, by ensuring that the sites content is not embedded into other sites.
        See [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options)
        for more information.
      items:
      - default: ""
        name: SAMEORIGIN
        title: SAMEORIGIN
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: DENY
        title: DENY
        value: ""
      - default: ""
        name: none
        title: none
        value: ""
      name: webapp_x_frame_options
      title: X-Frame-Options Header
      type: select_one
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      help_text: Sets additional URLs as allowed origins for the CORS policy and the
        CSRF filter. This option is used to allow browser based apps to call execution
        REST endpoints, e.g. for Service Deployments. Multiple URLs must be either
        newline or space separated, e.g. `http://localhost:9000 https://example.webapp.com`.
      name: execution_external_webapp_origins
      title: Whitelist URLs for Execution REST API
      type: textarea
      value: ""
    name: browser_security
    title: Browser Security
  - description: This section contains configuration options that are applied during
      the initial installation of KNIME Business Hub. These options will be hidden
      after the installation has completed, and any future changes will require an
      administrator to manually edit the affected resource(s).
    items:
    - default: knimeadmin
      help_text: The username for the admin user of KNIME Business Hub.
      name: knime_admin_username
      required: true
      title: KNIME Business Hub Admin Username
      type: text
      value: knimeadmin
    - default: ""
      help_text: The initial password for the admin user. This password can be changed
        in Keycloak post-installation.
      name: knime_admin_password
      required: true
      title: KNIME Business Hub Admin Password
      type: password
      value: ""
    - default: ""
      help_text: The name for the initial KNIME Business Hub Team.
      name: team_name
      title: Initial Team Name
      type: text
      value: Initial Team
    - default: ""
      name: team_name_invalid
      title: |-
        ***Invalid Team Name***
        Team name can only include letters and numbers as first character. Letters, numbers and underscore as last character. Letters, numbers, space, dot, underscore and hyphen for remaining characters. The minimum length is 3 characters, and the maximum length is 64 characters.
      type: label
      value: ""
      when: ''{{repl not (regexMatch "^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_. ]{1,62}[a-zA-Z0-9_]$"
        (ConfigOption "team_name")) }}''
    - default: ""
      help_text: The description for the initial KNIME Business Hub Team.
      name: team_description
      title: Initial Team Description
      type: text
      value: Initial Team created by KNIME
    - default: ""
      help_text: The name of the initial KNIME Business Hub Space (public) which will
        be associated with the initial KNIME Business Hub Team.
      name: team_space_name
      title: Initial Space Name
      type: text
      value: Initial Space
    - default: ""
      help_text: The name for the initial KNIME Business Hub Execution Context. This
        Execution Context is provisioned with minimal CPU/memory resources, and the
        resource allocation can be increased post-installation via the KNIME Business
        Hub REST API.
      name: execution_context_name
      title: Initial Execution Context Name
      type: text
      value: Initial Execution Context
      when: repl{{ ConfigOptionEquals "enable_execution_services" "1" }}
    - default: registry.hub.knime.com/knime/knime-full
      help_text: The image repository for the initial Execution Context.
      name: execution_context_image_repository
      title: Initial Execution Context Docker Image Repository
      type: text
      value: registry.hub.knime.com/knime/knime-full
      when: repl{{ ConfigOptionEquals "enable_execution_services" "1" }}
    - default: r-5.1.1-379
      help_text: The image tag for the initial Execution Context.
      name: execution_context_image_tag
      title: Initial Execution Context Docker Image Tag
      type: text
      value: r-5.1.1-379
    name: initialization
    title: Initialization of KNIME Business Hub
    when: repl{{ eq Sequence 0 }}
  - description: Enable or disable various services that KNIME Business Hub depends
      on.
    items:
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub Secret Operator syncs Kubernetes Secrets between
        multiple namespaces.
      name: enable_secret_operator
      title: Enable KNIME Business Hub Secret Operator
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub Infrastructure Layer contains critical architectural
        components of KNIME Business Hub. Depends on Istio, Secret Operator.
      name: enable_infrastructure
      title: Enable Infrastructure Layer
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Postgres Operator](https://postgres-operator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)
        manages Postgres deployments in the cluster.
      name: enable_postgres_operator
      title: Enable Postgres Operator
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [ActiveMQ Artemis service](https://activemq.apache.org/components/artemis/)
        is a message and event broker for services inside KNIME Business Hub.
      name: enable_artemis
      title: Enable ActiveMQ Artemis
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Redis service](https://redis.io/) is an in-memory data store
        for retaining KNIME Business Hub browser session caches.
      name: enable_redis
      title: Enable Redis
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Elasticsearch service](https://www.elastic.co/) is a JSON-based
        search and analytics engine which holds the search indices for KNIME Business
        Hub repository items.
      name: enable_elasticsearch
      title: Enable ElasticSearch
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Minio](https://min.io/) service is used for storing repository
        artifacts, either in-cluster or acting as a gateway cloud storage providers.
        Depends on Infrastructure Layer.
      name: enable_minio
      title: Enable Minio
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub Persistence Layer contains critical data persistence
        components of KNIME Business Hub. Depends on Postgres Operator, Infrastructure
        Layer.
      name: enable_persistence
      title: Enable Persistence Layer
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [Keycloak service](https://www.keycloak.org/) manages users and
        authentication for KNIME Business Hub. Depends on Persistence Layer.
      name: enable_keycloak
      title: Enable Keycloak
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The [NATS](https://docs.nats.io/) service is used for storing events
        that are used for various purposes.
      name: enable_nats
      title: Enable NATS
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub Application Layer contains the supporting
        architecture behind the KNIME Business Hub web application. Depends on All
        Of The Above.
      name: enable_hub_services
      title: Enable KNIME Business Hub Application Layer
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "1"
      help_text: The KNIME Business Hub Execution Services provide support for executing
        KNIME workflows. Depends on Application Layer.
      name: enable_execution_services
      title: Enable KNIME Business Hub Execution Services
      type: bool
      value: ""
    - default: "0"
      help_text: The KNIME Hub Secret Store provides a service to manage secrets that
        are consumed by KNIME workflows.
      name: enable_secret_store
      title: Enable KNIME Hub Secret Store
      type: bool
      value: ""
      when: repl{{ eq ( LicenseFieldValue "licenseType" ) "dev" }}
    name: services_and_dependencies
    title: Services and Dependencies
    when: repl{{ (ConfigOption "enable_advanced_settings" | ParseBool) }}
  - items:
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: accounts_notification_api_key
      title: Accounts Service API Key to be consumed by Notification Service
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: accounts_listing_api_key
      title: Accounts Service API Key for listing all accounts
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: accounts_creation_api_key
      title: Accounts Service API Key for creating accounts
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: catalog_write_nodes_and_extensions_api_key
      title: Catalog Service API Key for writing nodes and extensions.
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: catalog_full_read_access_api_key
      title: Catalog Service API Key for full read access.
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: catalog_management_api_key
      title: Catalog Service API Key for management endpoints.
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: webapp_cookie_sign_secret
      title: Cookie sign secret used by webapp.
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: webapp_session_encryption_secret
      title: Session encryption secret used by webapp. This needs to be a 32byte string.
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: artemis_user_credentials
      title: Credential string for user knime in artemis
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: minio_accounts_credentials
      title: Credential string for accounts-service user in minio
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: minio_catalog_credentials
      title: Credential string for catalog-service user in minio
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: vault_secret_store_credentials
      title: Credential string (secret_id) for the knime-hub-secret-store role in
        vault
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: minio_backup_credentials
      title: Credential string for postgres backups to Minio
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: auth_rely_cookie_secret_hash_key
      title: Cookie secret string (hashKey) used by auth-rely service
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 64}}''
    - default: ""
      hidden: true
      name: auth_rely_cookie_secret_block_key
      title: Cookie secret string (blockKey) used by auth-rely service
      type: text
      value: ''{{repl RandomString 32}}''
    name: generated_secrets
    title: ""
status: {}

kind: Backup
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: backup

INSERT INTO "app_version" VALUES('2XzB3rKi0QljeDzN32bEXzbyksY',1,'40','25Wg8fHYuNVbV82S6rcMlyRYQGh','Stable',NULL,1699876580,'1.7.0',0,'# KNIME Business Hub 1.7.0
## Important installation notes
Kubernetes version 1.25-1.27 is required for Business Hub 1.7.0. Pre-flight checks in the installer make sure that the correct version is available.
## Infrastructure and security updates
### Support provided ingress-nginx deployments
- In existing clusters creating own ingress-nginx deployments before the installation of Hub is now enabled. Wether the Hub install process deploys the inbuilt ingress-nginx can be configured on the Kots Admin dashboard.
### Security context update
- Security contexts updated for pods, containers and jobs in the hub, knime and knime-execution namespaces.
## Bugfixes
- Fixed a bug where schedules edited with KNIME Analytics Platform didn’t respect job discard settings.
- Fixed a bug where saving executed job as workflows didn’t work in case workflow size was larger than 50 MB.
- Fixed a bug where under certain circumstances jobs were shown duplicated in the AP explorer.
- Fixed a bug where schedules in all teams connected to a user were deactivated when the user left any team.
- Various smaller fixes.','apiVersion: troubleshoot.sh/v1beta2

','apiVersion: troubleshoot.sh/v1beta2
kind: Preflight
metadata:
  annotations:
    kots.io/exclude: "true"
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: preflight-checks
spec:
  analyzers:
  - clusterVersion:
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Kubernetes versions v1.25 - v1.27.
          uri: https://www.kubernetes.io
          when: ''>= 1.28.0''
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Kubernetes versions v1.25 - v1.27.
          uri: https://kubernetes.io
          when: < 1.25.0
      - pass:
          message: Your cluster meets the recommended and required versions of Kubernetes.
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: KOTS Admin Console Version
      fileName: static/kots-version
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports KOTS v1.101.2+. Please upgrade the
            KOTS based on the upgrade documentation.
          uri: https://docs.knime.com/latest/business_hub_installation_guide/index.html#_introduction
          when: "false"
      - pass:
          message: Your cluster meets the required version of KOTS.
          when: "true"
      regex: ^true$
  - containerRuntime:
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: Docker container runtime was found.
          when: == docker
      - pass:
          message: Containerd runtime was found.
          when: == containerd
      - pass:
          message: CRI-O runtime was found.
          when: == cri-o
      - fail:
          message: Did not find a viable container runtime (e.g. Docker).
  - distribution:
      checkName: Check Kubernetes environment.
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: The application does not support Microk8s clusters.
          when: == microk8s
      - warn:
          message: KNIME Business Hub supports Minikube clusters for testing only.
          when: == minikube
      - pass:
          message: EKS is a supported distribution.
          when: == eks
      - pass:
          message: GKE is a supported distribution.
          when: == gke
      - pass:
          message: AKS is a supported distribution.
          when: == aks
      - pass:
          message: K3s is a supported distribution.
          when: == k3s
      - pass:
          message: KURL is a supported distribution.
          when: == kurl
      - pass:
          message: Openshift is a supported distribution.
          when: == openShift
  - nodeResources:
      checkName: Total CPU Cores in the cluster is 16 or greater.
      outcomes:
      - fail:
          message: The cluster must contain at least 16 cores.
          when: sum(cpuCapacity) < 16
      - pass:
          message: There are at least 16 cores in the cluster.
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: PostgreSQL configuration
      fileName: static/postgres-settings
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: PostgreSQL configuration has no syntax errors.
          when: "true"
      - fail:
          message: PostgreSQL configuration has non-numeric values!
          when: "false"
      regex: ''[1-9][0-9]*;[1-9][0-9]*;[1-9][0-9]*''
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: KNIME Business Hub URL validation
      fileName: static/base-url
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: URL passes validation for alphanumeric and special characters.
          when: "true"
      - fail:
          message: Invalid URL. The URL cannot contain spaces or slashes /, and needs
            to have a top-level domain and at least one subdomain.
          when: "false"
      regex: ^[^\/ ]+\.[^\/ ]+$
  - textAnalyze:
      checkName: ''KNIME Business Hub URL validation: IP address''
      fileName: static/base-url
      outcomes:
      - pass:
          message: URL is not an IP address.
          when: "false"
      - fail:
          message: Invalid URL. The URL cannot be an IP address.
          when: "true"
      regex: ^(?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$
  collectors:
  - data:
      data: 200;1000;1024
      name: static/postgres-settings
  - data:
      data: hub.kbh-troubleshooting.com
      name: static/base-url
  - data:
      data: "true"
      name: static/kots-version
status: {}

    # KNIME Business Hub 1.7.0
    ## Important installation notes
    Kubernetes version 1.25-1.27 is required for Business Hub 1.7.0. Pre-flight checks in the installer make sure that the correct version is available.
    ## Infrastructure and security updates
    ### Support provided ingress-nginx deployments
    - In existing clusters creating own ingress-nginx deployments before the installation of Hub is now enabled. Wether the Hub install process deploys the inbuilt ingress-nginx can be configured on the Kots Admin dashboard.
    ### Security context update
    - Security contexts updated for pods, containers and jobs in the hub, knime and knime-execution namespaces.
    ## Bugfixes
    - Fixed a bug where schedules edited with KNIME Analytics Platform didn’t respect job discard settings.
    - Fixed a bug where saving executed job as workflows didn’t work in case workflow size was larger than 50 MB.
    - Fixed a bug where under certain circumstances jobs were shown duplicated in the AP explorer.
    - Fixed a bug where schedules in all teams connected to a user were deactivated when the user left any team.

    else}}{{repl end}}''
  - ''{{repl if ConfigOptionEquals "ingress_controller" "managed"}}knime/deployment/ingress-nginx-controller{{repl
    else}}{{repl end}}''
  - knime/statefulset/keycloak
  title: KNIME Business Hub
